title: Principles of processing
summary: Process personal data lawfully fairly and transparently; for specified purposes; minimised; accurate; kept no longer than needed; secure; and be able to show compliance (accountability).
typical_evidence: Records of processing showing purposes; retention schedule; privacy policy; data minimisation review

title: Lawfulness of processing
summary: Each processing activity has a lawful basis: consent; contract; legal obligation; vital interests; public task; or legitimate interests (with a balancing test).
typical_evidence: Lawful basis per processing activity in the records of processing; legitimate interest assessments

title: Conditions for consent
summary: Where consent is the basis: be able to show it was given; request it clearly and separately; allow withdrawal as easily as giving it; do not make services conditional on unnecessary consent.
typical_evidence: Consent records with timestamp and wording; withdrawal mechanism; cookie consent configuration

title: Child's consent for online services
summary: For information society services offered directly to children below the national age (13 to 16) get consent from the holder of parental responsibility and make reasonable efforts to verify it.
typical_evidence: Age gate; parental consent flow (only if services are offered to children)

title: Special categories of personal data
summary: Processing health; biometric; genetic; racial or ethnic; political; religious; trade union; sex life or orientation data is prohibited unless an Article 9(2) condition applies.
typical_evidence: Special category data inventory with Article 9 condition (only if processed)

title: Criminal convictions and offences data
summary: Process criminal offence data only under official authority or where Union or Member State law authorises it.
typical_evidence: Background check basis per country (only if processed)

title: Transparent communication and request handling
summary: Give information in concise plain language; facilitate rights; respond to requests within one month (extendable by two months); free of charge in principle.
typical_evidence: DSR procedure with timelines; DSR log with response dates

title: Information when data is collected from the person
summary: At collection provide identity and contact of the controller and DPO; purposes and lawful basis; recipients; transfers; retention; rights; right to complain.
typical_evidence: Privacy notice reviewed against Art 13 contents; notices at collection points

title: Information when data is not collected from the person
summary: Provide the same information plus the categories and source of the data within one month of obtaining it.
typical_evidence: Notice for indirectly obtained data (e.g. lead lists; customer-provided user data)

title: Right of access
summary: Confirm whether data is processed and give a copy plus the processing details.
typical_evidence: Access request procedure; sample responses

title: Right to rectification
summary: Correct inaccurate data and complete incomplete data without undue delay.
typical_evidence: Rectification procedure; DSR tickets

title: Right to erasure
summary: Erase data without undue delay when a listed ground applies (e.g. no longer needed; consent withdrawn; objection; unlawful) unless an exception applies.
typical_evidence: Erasure procedure; deletion job evidence; backups handling

title: Right to restriction of processing
summary: Restrict processing while accuracy or lawfulness is contested or when the person needs the data for legal claims.
typical_evidence: Restriction mechanism (flag or hold) and procedure

title: Notify recipients of rectification, erasure or restriction
summary: Tell each recipient of the data about rectification erasure or restriction unless impossible or disproportionate.
typical_evidence: Procedure to notify processors and recipients

title: Right to data portability
summary: Where processing is by automated means on consent or contract provide the data in a structured machine-readable format and transmit it where feasible.
typical_evidence: Export feature or procedure

title: Right to object
summary: Stop processing on objection where based on legitimate interests or public task unless compelling grounds; always stop for direct marketing.
typical_evidence: Objection handling procedure; marketing unsubscribe

title: Automated decision-making and profiling
summary: Do not subject people to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects unless an exception applies with safeguards (human review; contest).
typical_evidence: Inventory of automated decisions; human review process (only if used)

title: Responsibility of the controller
summary: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures and policies and be able to demonstrate compliance; review and update them.
typical_evidence: Data protection policy; privacy programme ownership; review records

title: Data protection by design and by default
summary: Build data protection into processing design and by default process only data necessary for each purpose.
typical_evidence: Privacy review in design or SDLC; default settings review

title: Joint controllers
summary: Joint controllers set out their responsibilities in an arrangement whose essence is available to data subjects.
typical_evidence: Joint controller arrangement (only if applicable)

title: EU representative
summary: Controllers or processors not established in the EU but subject to GDPR under Art 3(2) designate a representative in the EU in writing.
typical_evidence: Representative appointment (only if no EU establishment)

title: Processors
summary: Use only processors with sufficient guarantees; bind them by a contract with the Art 28(3) terms; processors need authorisation for sub-processors.
typical_evidence: DPAs with processors; sub-processor list and notifications; DPA template if acting as processor

title: Processing under the authority of the controller
summary: Processors and staff process personal data only on documented instructions.
typical_evidence: Confidentiality obligations; access restrictions; processor instructions

title: Records of processing activities
summary: Keep written records of processing as controller and as processor. The under-250-employee exemption is narrow and rarely applies to regular processing.
typical_evidence: Records of processing (controller and processor)

title: Cooperation with the supervisory authority
summary: Cooperate with the supervisory authority on request.
typical_evidence: Procedure and owner for regulator requests

title: Security of processing
summary: Implement security appropriate to the risk including as appropriate pseudonymisation and encryption; confidentiality integrity availability and resilience; restore capability; and regular testing of measures.
typical_evidence: Encryption settings; access control exports; backup and restore tests; penetration test; security policy

title: Breach notification to the supervisory authority
summary: Notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours unless unlikely to result in risk; document all breaches. Processors notify controllers without undue delay.
typical_evidence: Breach procedure with 72-hour clock; breach register; DPA clause for processor notification

title: Communication of a breach to data subjects
summary: When a breach is likely to result in high risk to people tell them without undue delay in plain language.
typical_evidence: Breach communication template and decision criteria

title: Data protection impact assessment
summary: Carry out a DPIA before processing likely to result in high risk (e.g. large-scale special category data; systematic monitoring; new technologies).
typical_evidence: DPIA screening; DPIAs for high-risk processing

title: Prior consultation
summary: Consult the supervisory authority before processing when a DPIA shows high residual risk.
typical_evidence: Consultation record (only if needed)

title: Designation of a DPO
summary: Designate a DPO when core activities involve large-scale regular and systematic monitoring or large-scale special category data (or public authority); publish contact details and inform the authority.
typical_evidence: DPO appointment or documented decision not to appoint; published contact

title: Position of the DPO
summary: Involve the DPO properly; ensure independence and resources; the DPO reports to the highest management level.
typical_evidence: DPO reporting line; involvement records

title: Tasks of the DPO
summary: The DPO informs and advises; monitors compliance; advises on DPIAs; cooperates with the authority.
typical_evidence: DPO activity reports

title: General principle for transfers
summary: Transfer personal data outside the EEA only under Chapter V conditions.
typical_evidence: Transfer inventory (subprocessor locations); transfer mechanism per transfer

title: Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision
summary: Transfers to countries with an adequacy decision (including the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for certified US companies) need no further authorisation.
typical_evidence: List of transfers relying on adequacy; DPF certification check

title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
summary: Without adequacy use safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses with a transfer impact assessment.
typical_evidence: Signed SCCs; transfer impact assessments

title: Binding corporate rules
summary: Intra-group transfers may rely on BCRs approved by the competent authority.
typical_evidence: Approved BCRs (only if used)

title: Derogations for specific situations
summary: Without adequacy or safeguards transfers are allowed only under narrow derogations such as explicit consent or necessity for a contract.
typical_evidence: Derogation analysis (only if relied on)
